thread:
alyssa: heads up — we've started seeing intermittent 502s to partner-api in eu-central3 this morning. symptoms point to SNAT port exhaustion on the central NAT gateway after the route-table segmentation rollout. connection traces show a ton of short-lived outbound connections from workers-ml-* to partner-api:443 :grimacing:

sanjay: can you paste the exact project/route config? are we still using the single central NAT (central-egress-nat) for all envs?

alyssa: yes central-egress-nat in project redwood-prod-eu, region europe-central3. we have 3 subnets for ML workers (workers-ml-1/2/3) that were just given distinct route tables to steer traffic via the new transit router. terraform snippet below (sanitized):

```
resource "google_compute_route" "workers_ml_to_transit" {
  name       = "rt-workers-ml-to-transit"
  network    = var.vpc
  dest_range = "0.0.0.0/0"
  next_hop_vpn_tunnel = google_compute_vpn_tunnel.transit.id
  priority = 1000
}
```

The router is set up with Cloud NAT that currently uses 2 external IPs (~64k ports each), but we still see port exhaustion.

infra-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-5927 — "eu-central3 Cloud NAT port exhaustion after route-table segmentation". Link: https://tickets.internal/INFRA-5927 :ticket:

mike: quick thoughts — 2 IPs -> ~128k ports, but real-world ephemeral port exhaustion happens sooner due to many short connections + connection tracking. options, in order of impact/cost:
- add more external IPs to Cloud NAT (easy, immediate)
- request increased per-IP port quota from cloud provider (if available)
- enable connection reuse / connection pooling at app level (longer term)
- migrate partner traffic to Private Service Connect/PrivateLink (removes NAT entirely)

also confirm: are these worker pods creating tons of outbound connections per inference request? if so batching/keepalives will help.

alyssa: they are calling partner for small telemetry on each request, ~10-20 concurrent short TCP conns per pod. will follow up with app team about keepalive. in parallel, we need a fast infra mitigation.

olga: +1 on adding external IPs. i'd request 6 -> 8 IPs in eu-central3 for central-egress-nat and also ask cloud for a higher ephemeral port allocation if they can. note there's also a hard limit on the number of NAT IPs per router in some regions. i've seen providers cap to 16 without special support.

kelsey: cost/ops note — adding IPs increases egress NAT SKU and static IP charges. estimate: ~€0.02/hour/IP + per-GB egress. we'll need cost sign-off if this stays long term.

mike: small commands if we want to reserve more IPs now (gcloud):
```
# reserve 6 more static addresses
for i in {1..6}; do gcloud compute addresses create nat-extra-$i --region europe-central3; done
# update router NAT config
gcloud compute routers nats update central-router --region=europe-central3 --nat-all-subnet-ip-ranges --nat-external-ip-pool=projects/redwood-prod-eu/regions/europe-central3/addresses/nat-external-1,projects/.../nat-extra-1,...
```

alyssa: i'll open the cloud quota request now and attach the ticket INFRA-5927. also quick ask: while i'm in there, can we also request extra GPU quota for dedicated-cluster-redwood-prod-eu? we want to scale Dedicated pools next week: need +8 A100s (on-demand) in europe-central3. separate approval but would be great to bundle.

sanjay: include the GPU SKU and justification in the same cloud support case — faster to have a single case for region resource increases. provide CI/CD timestamps for expected rollout and any commitments to delete if not used.

olga: also considering a more durable design: mark partner API traffic route to a dedicated egress cluster with its own NAT (per-team NAT) so noisy tenants don't affect global NAT. tradeoff is more IPs and slightly more infra to manage.

kelsey: agree with isolating noisy egress. short-term: add 6 IPs + open provider quota for ephemeral ports + request 8 A100 GPU quota in same case. long-term: propose a roadmap item to split egress or negotiate PSC with partner.

alyssa: thanks — i'll: 1) reserve IPs, 2) update NAT config, 3) open cloud case with INFRA-5927 and request ephemeral port bump + 8 A100s, 4) file a follow-up RFC for per-team NAT. will post updates here. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: INFRA-5927 updated: cloud case submitted (case #C-334221). provider ETA 48-72h.

mike: if provider is slow, we can temporarily spin a regional egress fleet in a separate project with its own NAT + peering to avoid cross-tenant blast radius. planning note for later.

alyssa: copied. i'll coordinate with app team on keepalives and will update the ticket with traffic samples. thanks everyone.
